name: Computer User Interface Understanding. A New Dataset and a Learning Framework
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces desktop interaction videos and a framework combining synthetic examples with hierarchical contrastive learning for interface classification.

name: AgentStudio: A Toolkit for Building General Virtual Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: AgentStudio combines an interactive GUI/API environment with tools for creating tasks, annotating interface elements, and labeling actions in videos. Its online suite and GroundUI, IDMBench, and CriticBench datasets examine interaction, grounding, learning from video, and success detection.

notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces video-based GUI questions and annotations for studying temporal interface understanding across varied interaction settings.

summary: Introduces WONDERBREAD, a benchmark pairing human WebArena workflow demonstrations with screen recordings, action logs, and written procedures. Six evaluation tasks cover documentation, knowledge transfer, and process improvement beyond end-to-end execution.

notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces Act2Cap and a cursor-guided method for describing GUI actions from video, with temporal and spatial localization challenges.

name: VideoWebArena: Evaluating Long Context Multimodal Agents with Video Understanding Web Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Evaluates whether web agents can retain procedural skills and factual information from long video tutorials and use them during tasks.

name: Mobile-Agent-V: A Video-Guided Approach for Effortless and Efficient Operational Knowledge Injection in Mobile Automation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced. The authors identify arXiv:2505.13887 as an accidental duplicate and direct future updates to this record.
summary: Extracts operational guidance from video for mobile task execution and introduces Mobile-Knowledge to evaluate the contribution of external knowledge.

name: BEARCUBS: A benchmark for computer-using web agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: BEARCUBS provides 111 live-web information-seeking questions with short answers and human-validated browsing trajectories. Its tasks require multimodal computer interaction, including video understanding and navigation of interactive 3D content.

name: GUI-Xplore: Empowering Generalizable GUI Agents with One Exploration
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces GUI-Xplore exploration videos and downstream tasks, with an agent that combines action-aware modeling and graph-based environment reasoning.

name: TongUI: Internet-Scale Trajectories from Multimodal Web Tutorials for Generalized GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: TongUI converts multimodal online tutorials, including videos and articles, into GUI-agent trajectories. Its GUI-Net dataset contains 143,000 trajectories spanning five operating systems and more than 200 applications, and supports fine-tuning for grounding and navigation.

name: Scalable Video-to-Dataset Generation for Cross-Platform Mobile Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces MONDAY and an automated pipeline that extracts mobile-navigation training data from instructional videos across operating-system platforms.

name: VideoCAD: A Dataset and Model for Learning Long-Horizon 3D CAD UI Interactions from Video
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces synthetic CAD interaction videos, a model for learning interface actions from video, and evaluation tasks for spatial and long-horizon reasoning.

name: VideoAgentTrek: Computer Use Pretraining from Unlabeled Videos
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Extracts structured GUI actions from screen-recorded tutorials using inverse dynamics, then uses the inferred trajectories for computer-use training.

name: Learning from Online Videos at Inference Time for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract. Experiments and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: This work retrieves online video tutorials and converts them into structured GUI action demonstrations with short objectives. A two-stage selection process supplies a relevant local trajectory as in-context guidance at each execution step.

name: Video-Based Reward Modeling for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Builds ExeVR-53k from execution-video, instruction and reward triplets, including negative instructions with step annotations. A reward model uses spatiotemporal token pruning to judge task completion from the instruction and execution keyframes.

name: Ego2Web: A Web Agent Benchmark Grounded in Egocentric Videos
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Ego2Web pairs first-person videos with online tasks that require agents to connect the user’s physical context to web actions. It also evaluates an automatic task judge against human judgments and analyzes failures in video understanding and web execution.

name: CUA-Suite: Massive Human-annotated Video Demonstrations for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: CUA-Suite combines continuous expert desktop demonstrations in VideoCUA with the UI-Vision evaluation benchmark and GroundCUA grounding data. Screen recordings, cursor traces and layered annotations support study of temporal behavior and professional software workflows.

name: GUIDE: A Benchmark for Understanding and Assisting Users in Open-Ended GUI Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: GUIDE evaluates whether models can recognize a user’s behavior, infer intent and decide when to offer help during open-ended software tasks. It uses narrated screen recordings of novice users and studies the effect of additional user context on these assistance decisions.

name: GUIDE: Resolving Domain Bias in GUI Agents through Real-Time Web Video Retrieval and Plug-and-Play Annotation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: GUIDE retrieves relevant software tutorials through subtitle-based video search, then infers planning and grounding knowledge from consecutive annotated keyframes. It inserts that knowledge into existing GUI-agent modules without parameter updates and evaluates the plug-in on OSWorld.

name: MolmoPoint: Better Pointing for VLMs with Grounding Tokens
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified. Adjacent general VLM pointing method with an explicit GUI-grounding experiment; no autonomous GUI-task execution is established.
summary: MolmoPoint replaces textual coordinate generation with pointing tokens that select visual regions and refine them through subpatches. The general image/video method includes GUI-pointing evaluation on ScreenSpotPro alongside other visual grounding tasks.

name: Benchmarking and Improving GUI Agents in High-Dynamic Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces DynamicGUIBench for applications whose interfaces change between actions, together with DynamicUI, an agent that processes screen recordings. The agent selects informative frames, filters inconsistent action reasoning and uses trajectory reflection for subsequent decisions.

name: Beyond Screenshots: Evaluating VLMs' Understanding of UI Animations
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.
summary: AniMINT evaluates how VLMs perceive, explain and interpret UI animations using densely annotated videos. The study distinguishes basic motion recognition from higher-level animation meaning and probes motion, context and perceptual cues.

name: MMTB: Evaluating Terminal Agents on Multimedia-File Tasks
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified. Adjacent computer-automation benchmark using terminal workflows, explicitly separated from graphical-interface control.
summary: MultiMedia-TerminalBench evaluates agents that use terminal tools to work with audio and video files. The Terminus-MM harness adds multimedia perception to study how accessible evidence changes executable workflows and task outcomes.

name: OmniGUI: Benchmarking GUI Agents in Omni-Modal Smartphone Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: OmniGUI evaluates step-level action prediction from interleaved smartphone screenshots, synchronous audio and video. Expert demonstrations carry multimodal-dependency annotations, and initial baselines use native multimodal models as agent proxies to study temporal and audio-related failures.

name: Benchmarking Living-Screen-Native GUI Agents on Short-Video Platforms
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: LivingScreen evaluates agents in a browser-based short-video environment where observing content consumes time and affects subsequent actions. Its task suite scores accuracy together with information efficiency to diagnose over- and under-observation on continuously changing screens.

name: Agent-Computer Observation Interfaces Enable Dynamic Computer Use
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: The Agent-Computer Observation Interface separates continuous perception from discrete computer actions using captured frames, audio transcription and persistent visual narration. DynaCU-Bench tests these components on dynamic browser tasks and static controls, with model-specific ablations showing that additional observations can also hurt.

name: DigitalCoach: Communication and Grounding Gaps in Human and Agentic Computer Use Coaching
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: DigitalCoach records expert–novice software coaching conversations aligned with screen and input events. Automated and interactive evaluations examine how model coaches differ from humans in explanation, error diagnosis and visual grounding when helping a learner operate software.

name: Invisible in Space, Visible in Time: Motion Vision CAPTCHA against GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: MVCAP-Bench tests live browser CAPTCHAs whose foreground meaning emerges through motion against dynamic backgrounds. A foreground-only control separates temporal camouflage difficulty from answer format and browser interaction.

name: MONDAY annotations
notes: The ungated Hub publishes four Parquet splits containing video identifiers and annotations. Original videos and extracted screenshots must be obtained separately; the code README explains that consumers download source videos from YouTube. A Windows Mobile unseen-OS test split is documented but is not labeled desktop Windows here. The companion code has an Apache-2.0 file, while the data card declares no data license and the repository defers third-party materials to original terms. Training scripts, pretrained checkpoints and the full generation pipeline remain planned updates.
summary: Video-derived mobile navigation annotations that pair scene boundaries and screen or element boxes with action labels for training and evaluating GUI agents.
